description.text:
The 53 promotional cards Wizards of the Coast numbered between July 1999 and March 2003, each with a black star reading PROMO where the expansion symbol would go, which gave Black Star Promos their name.

Most were monthly Pokémon League prizes, from the Pikachu of July 1999 to the Snorlax of August 2002. The films brought others: Electabuzz, Mewtwo, Pikachu and Dragonite at screenings of Pokémon: The First Movie from November 1999, with a gold stamp reading "Kids WB Presents: Pokémon: The First Movie" on the art; Articuno, Moltres and Zapdos for The Power of One, with art different from their Japanese promos; Entei for Spell of the Unown; and Celebi for Pokémon 4Ever, with more cards in the home video releases. Nintendo added its own, in Nintendo Power magazine, the Game Boy Trading Card Game and the Pokémon Stadium bundle, and the opening of Pokémon Center New York in November 2001 brought the Pokémon Center and Lucky Stadium cards.

Every card had come out in Japan first, as a promo or in a special set, except the two Mew (8 and 9), which came from the Japanese Fossil expansion. The set ended when Wizards lost its license.

This copy carries a stamp added by LPPCollecting, an Italian card shop and distributor that runs Pokémon tournaments and Pokémon Days in Italy. It is not an official Pokémon stamp. This one reads "LPPCollecting – Per 2 o piu' giogatori", a misspelling of the Italian for "for 2 or more players", and was given out at the Italian Pokémon Day at Mirabilandia on 18 and 19 June 2011. LPPCollecting's own listing counts 1,191 printed.

When the misspelling was noticed the stamp was corrected to "giocatori" (243 printed, by the same listing), and a version worded in English was made around the same time. Upside-down copies of both Italian stamps exist (57 and 6), and from December 2021 LPPCollecting gave a "20th Anniversario" stamped copy with larger orders from its webshop, for its twentieth anniversary.

This copy is the Pokémon The First Movie promo, gold "Kids WB Presents" stamp and all, printed in Japan on Japanese card stock. description.text:
_____'s Pikachu, better known as Birthday Pikachu: the blank is for its owner's name, and its attack Birthday Surprise can do 50 more damage on your birthday. Every player who entered Wizards of the Coast's first fan card contest, Create a Baby Pokémon, got one. The contest was a League activity of the second year, open to players who had earned the first badge. Each could design one new Baby Pokémon card; Gym Leaders mailed the entry sheets to Wizards, which sent back the same number of Birthday Pikachus with a thank-you letter. Wizards received far more entries than it expected, and the cards took much longer to arrive than it had estimated.

Kagemaru Himeno drew it. A copy with a Pikachu tail stamp came in the Pikachu World Collection, sold only at Pokémon Park 2000 at the University of Sydney between 12 September and 4 October 2000, alongside the Sydney Olympics.
